item.title: Who Watches the Watchers? Trust and Accountability in Software Development
item.description: I left an earlier startup environment partly because I feared its people, workload, and working conditions would lead me to burnout. I burnt out anyway while balancing engineering work with part-time schooling. My life outside work was changing, too: I had been through a breakup, and family relationships and responsibilities were shifting. I mention this as context for my own capacity at the time, not as an explanation of anyone else’s conduct at work.

item.title: Sovereignty Is Having an Exit
item.description: A practical view of digital sovereignty built around portability, rebuildability, and keeping services replaceable rather than trying to self-host everything.

item.title: Testing an Agentic Governance Boundary: 7 + 27 + 24 Anthesis Scenarios
item.description: Anthesis Governance Lab separates three public proof surfaces: 7 canonical policy cases, 9 packs with 27 broader governance scenarios, and 24 deterministic inference-integrity cases.

item.title: The Tubes, or Whatever
item.description:
The funny thing is, everybody keeps saying we’re in the foothills. That kills me. The foothills. Like we’re all on some healthy little hike with trail mix and expensive boots and somebody’s dad checking the map.

We’re not in the foothills. We’re in the tubes.

item.title: CareerOps: Building a Governed AI-Assisted Job Application Pipeline
item.description: How a false-precision resume failure led to a governed CareerOps pipeline built around canonical truth, evidence classes, GitHub issues, local execution, and human submission.

item.title: Git Is Becoming an Execution Surface
item.description: Why branch names, commit metadata, and other Git inputs should be treated as untrusted data once automation, shells, and privileged runtimes start interpreting them.

item.title: Anthesis Update: Memory, Governance, and Beyond the SDLC
